about: Fault counts the gates in tool/ are held to. Read by tool/check_gates.py, which fails when a gate's count moves in either direction: up means a new fault, down means a baseline that should be lowered so the repair sticks. 'measured' is the date the count last changed. Regenerate with `python3 tool/check_gates.py --update`; write 'note' by hand.

check_api_reference.note: Zero: every package's doc/api/ reads clean, and UNWRITTEN is empty. tom_flutter_ui (1153 faults in detail) and tom_core_agentic (370) were the last two, brought to the standard by tool/fill_api_reference.py, which writes what this gate finds missing from the source and its dartdoc -- five whole summaries (groups, theme, widgets, bearer_auth, mcp_auth), Source lists as full paths, Global Functions tables, index rows and member rows -- plus hand repairs in the ACL summary: its method-group headings renamed into member headings (`Methods -- structure`), so the members listed under them count for their class, and its Global Functions table given a name column. Two readings were the gate's: a `part` file's declarations are now exported with the library that names it, and the ACL module was reached through a forwarder at lib/src/ the barrel no longer uses. tom_core_server was zero from the first run, which is how the port is known to read as the server's own suite does; the kernel opened at 103 and tom_core_flutter at 32, both repaired rather than baselined.

check_api_signatures.note: Lands at zero over six packages (598 fences, 658 members compared) after its first run found 27 signatures that disagreed with the code and they were repaired in the same pass: five exceptions quoting `bool? serverCallError` for a `TomServerCallError?` parameter, three `autoLog = true` defaults that are `false`, a preference-key exception quoted with a parameter list it no longer has, a `progress` quoted as `Widget?` that is a `double?`, a missing `const`, a constructor type parameter, three OAuth defaults quoted as `''`, a constructor of a type the package does not export, and all 21 constructor fences of tom_core_codespecs' summary, cut off before their closing `})`. The checker's own false positives were fixed before any page was touched: typedef, raw-generic, record and named-function-type spellings are compared structurally, positional parameters by position, and a qualified or private default is accepted. Zero is the steady state; the gate exists for recurrence.

check_barrel_exports.note: Lands at zero because all four faults it found were legitimate omissions, and each was declared with a marker in its barrel in the same pass: reflection_seed.dart in advanced_client_core, reflection_entry.dart in todo_domain, and the two generated colour/icon tables behind tom_colors.dart and tom_icons.dart in tom_flutter_ui. Zero is the expected steady state -- the gate exists for recurrence, not backlog, and the one defect of this class (session_two_factor_controller.dart, absent from advanced_app_client's app.dart) was already repaired by tcinc947. 39 barrels across 23 packages are in scope. A directory with no barrel is deliberately not covered: the six Flutter sample applications correctly re-export nothing from screens/ and groups/, and demanding it would produce some ninety faults, all wrong.

check_baseline_claims.note: Zero. The first run judged 86 past-tense claims whose subject is a backticked Tom* symbol, inside the What changed sections of 49 *_changes.md documents, against the 864 Tom* identifiers present at 3bdb9f0. It found 8 naming a symbol the baseline did not have -- descriptions of intermediate states, which the completion contract forbids in part 3: the preferences document's all() and clear narratives, two replay-store rows of the logging table (moved into part 1 as current guarantees), TomLoginException 'moved' (it is new), and two endpoints sentences. All were restated; the next one is a failure. The rule decides only claims about symbols that did not exist at all; prose narrating an intermediate state of a symbol that did exist is out of its reach.

check_comments_read_as_is.note: Zero across every package in tom_ai/core, figures included. The gate refuses work-item ids (matched by shape against a closed vocabulary of English and published technical words, never by a quest-prefix list, which fails open) and history narration: past-indicative statements about the code's own earlier states, including `as before`, `formerly`, a sentence-initial `Previously` and `used to <verb>`. `used to` in the employed-in-order-to sense is matched too when its verb is one the rule lists, so such a sentence is rewritten rather than exempted; that false-positive shape is the cost of a rule that does not leak. The last 28 sites, in tom_flutter_ui and tom_flutter_form_test, were rewritten on 2026-10-07 into present-tense statements of the rule or the hazard; the next one to arrive is a failure.

check_dart_format.note: Zero, and it must stay there: the fix is never a code change, it is `python3 tool/check_dart_format.py --fix`. 1537 files across 23 packages. It landed at zero only because the four drifted files it found on the day -- all in tom_flutter_form_test, a package with no guard -- were formatted in the same pass. Two packages carry their own in-suite `formatting_test.dart` and keep it; this covers the other 21, which had nothing. If it fails where nothing was edited, the SDK's formatter changed its output: reformat and commit that alone, and do not raise this.

check_dartdoc_build.note: Zero, and held there. `dart doc` must report neither a warning nor an error for tom_core_kernel, tom_core_agentic or tom_core_codespecs. Every fault is one bracketed name in one comment, so a rise of one is a real regression rather than noise -- this count was 11 for tom_core_kernel alone before the gate existed.

The test now produces its own JSON in-process and asserts the round trip, which is the question worth asking; the file, its inert `tom_analyzer` builder configuration and the exemptions three guards carried for it went with it. The six files this gate was written for -- three doc/last_testrun.json captures and three doc/baseline_*.csv -- were removed when it landed. Zero is the steady state: doc/ is hand-authored, and a tool's output belongs where it can be regenerated without a commit.

check_doc_dart_blocks.note: Lands at zero because the 14 faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass, across 11 tom_core_kernel documents. Zero here does not mean the tree is clean: only tom_core_kernel is in PACKAGES, and doc/api_reference/ is excluded within it. tom_core_server reports 19 when run with its name as an argument, tom_flutter_ui and tom_core_flutter have not been surveyed -- see tcextension7_aico-doc-dart-blocks-other-packages.

check_doc_dependencies.note: Lands at zero because the 28 faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass. Eleven of the 15 package completion documents carried a Dependencies section and seven of those were incomplete; the four remaining package documents (advanced_app_server, advanced_auth_server, advanced_ops_server, core_server_sample) had no section at all and were written, so a missing section is a NOSECTION fault rather than a skip -- a gate you can pass by deleting the section is not a gate. Every one of the 28 omissions was a build-time entry (build, build_runner, tom_reflection_generator, lints, test, flutter_test, flutter_lints) while the runtime half was complete in every case. Module documents are skipped: a document is audited only when its opening inventory resolves to a directory carrying a pubspec.yaml.

check_doc_error_keys.note: Zero: every hand-written module guide under tom_core_*/doc/ names every error key its module raises, each beside the condition that produces it rather than in a list at the foot of the guide. The gate opened at 330 the first time it read those guides -- until then it audited only the completion documents, and only sections headed exactly `Error keys`, so it reported the guides clean by never looking. The backlog was written down guide by guide (tcextension23_aihi). The one completion-document fault it began with, `storage.blob.exists`, was never a key: a table wrote "`TomBlobStore.describe` and `.exists`" and the gate read the bare `.exists` as a sibling key; the table now names `TomBlobStore.exists` in full. A key named only by a wildcard or an elided prefix does not count, so a guide that writes a family must spell its members.

check_doc_inventories.note: Zero because all 94 faults were repaired by `--fix` in one pass. The repair was forced: the repo-wide `dart format` of tcincb1_ahti reflowed 777 Dart files, and an INDEX/HEADER/LINES claim is measured against the module's source line totals, not against the wording of the document -- so the reflow invalidated 46 figures on top of the 48 already stale here. `--fix` cannot repair only the 46: a figure is right or wrong, so the same pass also discharged the 48 that tcfinal1_aicl_stale_module_header_figures owned. 33 documents, 90 substitutions, every line identical in length before and after, so no line needed re-wrapping. Adding or retiring a table row still needs a hand, because a new row needs a sentence saying what the file carries. Still zero after the LAYOUT widening, which checks every layout-tree row's file for existence rather than only the rows that also claim a length: 264 rows across 16 documents, all present, and one more document audited (tom_core_samples_assets_new.md, whose drawn tree of 9 SVGs is the only inventory it has). Still zero after the PROSE widening, which reports a length figure sitting in a position no other audit read. It is instrumented rather than pattern-matched: each audit records the spans it took a length out of and PROSE reports the leftovers, so the census and index sentences -- prose, but read -- stay covered and widening any audit narrows PROSE automatically. It found 28 unchecked measurements across 14 documents, including `Eight steps, one file, 239 lines` of a file that had been 250 for four commits; all 28 were removed by rewriting the sentence rather than by restating the number, since a length nothing maintains is worse than no length. `--fix` does not repair PROSE: the number is usually right and what is wrong is where it sits.

check_doc_kinds.note: Zero since 2964a5ec (2026-09-03), which rewrote all 132 Kind cells across 23 documents to name the declaration verbatim -- 'exception', 'annotation', 'entity', 'widget' and the like became 'class', and 'interface'/'abstract' became the 'abstract class' or 'abstract interface class' the source declares. No information was dropped: the 32 cells that also carried a fact (@tomReflector, an annotation's argument, 'statics only', 'const', a getter's type) had it moved into the Purpose column. 957 kind claims checked as of 2026-09-29.

check_doc_links.note: Lands at zero because the 90 faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass: 84 ABSOLUTE links to /_copilot_guidelines/ in the 14 _copilot_guidelines/ files of this repo, 4 DEAD ../tom_core_*/ links written one level too shallow in the kernel's and server's index.md, 1 DEAD api_summary_result.md for a Result module the kernel does not have, and 1 GUIDELINE link out of tom_flutter_ui/README.md. The ABSOLUTE shape was workspace-wide -- 371 links in 70 files across tom_ai, tom_assistant, tom_sqm, tom_uam and the global _copilot_guidelines/ -- all repaired in the same pass, and its source, the index.md template in _copilot_guidelines/dart/new_project_setup.md, was corrected so the count stops growing by one table per new project. Anchors are out of scope (check_doc_tocs owns headings) and so are external URLs. Still zero after the REFERENCE widening, which reports a bracketed inline code span carrying no target and no definition -- dartdoc's square-bracket syntax in a markdown file, which renders as literal brackets. The rule lives here rather than in its own gate because this gate was blind to it BY CONSTRUCTION: the link scan looks for `](` and runs after inline code is blanked, and the label of one of these IS the code span, so the line reads `[      ]` by the time it is read; a reference with no definition also has no target for a link-resolving checker to fail on. Thirty-four sat across four packages while this file read 0 -- 18 in one tom_flutter_ui page, 9 in a tom_core_agentic page no scan had opened, and the 3 that were actually filed. All 34 were repaired in the same pass by dropping the brackets, because not one of them had an anchor it could have pointed at. Only bracketed CODE SPANS are matched: a bare `[Some Name]` is English punctuation far more often than a broken link. A double-backtick span is blanked first, which is reading markdown correctly rather than an exemption: that form exists to CONTAIN backticks, so it is how a document quotes the shape the rule forbids -- without it this README, the four CHANGELOG entries and the gate's own docstring would each be an instance of what they describe. Eight planted cases check the rule: two positives (one reference, and two on one line) and six controls -- a real inline link, a reference with a definition, one inside a fence, one quoted in a double-backtick span, an unbackticked bracket pair, and `operator [](Object? key)` inside a span, which is the false positive this gate's own docstring warned about.

check_doc_overview_types.note: Zero from the day it landed. Nineteen of the twenty faults it found were one row in tom_flutter_ui/doc/widget_base.md eliding twenty branch bases behind an ellipsis, which is exactly the curation the exhaustive rule forbids; the row now names them. 31 documents and 569 public types are in scope. Zero is the expected steady state: the gate exists for recurrence, and a fault is repaired by adding the row, never by narrowing the scope.

Frozen, not zero: most are legitimate -- unbuilt parts of design documents that say they are partially implemented, migration notes naming what they migrated from, the forms specification's divergence table, prefix families such as TomCupertinoForm and TomN. The five phantoms that motivated the gate (TomFormErrorDisplay, TomFormErrorSnackbar, TomFormErrorInline, TomFormErrorList, TomMasterDetailScaffold, seven occurrences) were removed before it was baselined, so the count starts from a forms specification that names only types that exist. Lower it as entries are repaired; never raise it -- a new phantom is a name the documentation invented. Lowered 218 -> 216 when tom_flutter_ui's design documents were triaged for check_doc_dart_blocks: samples still showing the retired TomGroupScope and TomUIResources were rewritten to the shipped API. Lowered from 216 on 2026-10-08: three occurrences of `TomFileRef` stopped being phantoms when tom_flutter_ui's last unprefixed exports were renamed and `FileRef` became `TomFileRef`.

check_doc_samples.note: Zero. The eight faults this baseline recorded were all in two tom_flutter_ui design documents, and all in blocks written against an API the framework never had: form fields called with `tomId:` named and a `binding:` parameter that does not exist, an enum dropdown given `items:` where the shipped parameter is `source:`, `saveAll()` for `save()`, and a `TomColumn<Order>('name', ...)` table column colliding with the shipped `TomColumn`, which is a layout column taking named parameters only. Correcting the eight calls alone would have silenced the gate while leaving both blocks uncompilable, so the sections around them were rewritten against the real API and modelled on compiled code. 3443 samples in 245 documents, 2064 constructors indexed in 23 packages. The 14 'documents unplaced' are unchanged: 13 tom_core_samples READMEs and the completion index, none of which names a single package.

check_doc_tocs.note: Zero is the steady state. The gate covers every anchor a document links to: within itself (a [§10](#stale-anchor) in running prose, not only contents entries -- check_doc_links accepts any #fragment and names this gate as the one that decides) and, since 2026-10-08, into another document (CROSS: other.md#fragment, resolved to the target's heading slugs plus its explicit <a id>/<a name> anchors). CROSS opened at one real fault, repaired rather than baselined: the server's authentication summary linked TomLoginFailure in its own little_things summary after the enum had moved to the kernel's security summary. A target not on disk is left to check_doc_links (DEAD). 274 documents are scanned; 128 carry a table of contents and are additionally held to listing every ## section, in document order. --self-test plants each CROSS case in memory and misspells one real cross-document link.

check_downstream_consumers.note: Zero. It landed at 10, every one in tom_uam_client's regenerated lib/00_main.reflection.dart: five constructor closures for bounded generics (NumRange, TomObservableEnum, TomCupertinoFormEnumSegmented, HitTestEntry, DateTimeRange), two diagnostics each. The cause was the consumer's language version, not the closures alone: tom_uam_client declares sdk >=3.0.0, and below Dart 3.7 inference picks dynamic for a bounded type parameter fed dynamic arguments. tom_reflection_generator 1.8.0 instantiates such classes at their bounds (NumRange<num>(low, high)), and tom_uam_client's constraint was raised to >=1.8.0 and its mirror regenerated (tcfinalb2_aißi). The server's seven missing TomLoginException reasons and its eight stale-reflection errors, the failure this gate exists for, were repaired earlier (tcfinal25_aipe); restoring them reads 15.

check_flutter_platform_step.note:
Lands at zero because all seven faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass: every Flutter sample under tom_core_samples/ said `flutter run` and tracked no platform folder, so the documented command could not start. Each README now names `flutter create --empty --platforms=

.` before its first fenced `flutter run`, and each .gitignore lists the six platform folders and .metadata. Verified, not assumed: for all seven, the step was run in place and `flutter run -d macos --machine` reached app.started, and the step wrote no file git would track. The two harnesses commit their platform folders and are out of scope by that test, not by name.

A count above zero is the SDK moving: regenerate with the generators' own command and read the diff for removed keys before committing it.

check_member_attributions.note: Lands at zero because every fault it found on its first repo-wide run was repaired in the same pass. The subject was tom_flutter_ui_test/doc/widget_resource_parameters.md, whose resolver table named seven methods that existed nowhere and attributed the rest to TomNodeBase, which declares no resolvers; the 1,181 references were requalified onto TomCtr and TomStyleResolvers, the types the widgets actually call. That exposed eight more across four other documents, each a single wrong name -- TomTotp2FAService.encodeBase32 for generateSecret, TomBool.value for get(), TomFormStyle.requiredIndicator for the field it is declared on, TomAclBuilder.setBpMinWidth for addRowBreakpoint, TomField.formName/fieldName for TomForm.formId and TomField.tomId, and TomDbType.of for the of() the subclasses carry. A rise means a document now names a member its type does not declare; a fall means a member was deleted or renamed and the baseline should follow it down. Widened 2026-09-29 to hold member names in the completion corpus to the declarations they describe: the gate now reads _ai/quests/tom_core/completion/ as a second root; reads member tables (a Member/Method/Field/Property/Constructor column) against the type their lead-in or nearest type heading names, accepting a row if any named candidate declares it (or takes it as a constructor parameter, or declares it at top level in that package's lib/); skips a completion document's part 3 history except 'What is still open', and any document opening with a '<!-- record: why -->' comment; and completes inheritance closures through the Dart SDK's public libraries, so a type extending DateTime is judged rather than abstained on. Attributions read rose from 2,483 to 7,774. The widening found real drift and all of it was repaired in the same pass: TomUser.timeZone and TomGetSettingsResult.clientTimeZone (renamed to timezone/clientTimezone; the settings rename is now recorded in part 3 and the missing server-side timezone added), TomServerEndpoint.removeLeadingSlash (deleted 2026-08-17), TomTotp2FAService.encodeBase32 (generateSecret), TomForm.authorizationGroup (renamed tomGroup), the TomReportResult API summary (its property table was the section's), and formstyle_migration.md, whose Part 1 still called the retired flat TomFormStyle 'current' and is now a declared record. Replaying the incident that motivated it -- convertToTimezone back in the TomZonedDate method table -- is reported.

check_module_dependencies.note: Zero. The two it stood at were tom_core_agentic's `agent` and `llm` modules having no document at all; both now have one, and both stated their dependencies in prose rather than the table this gate parses. Writing the tables showed why the shape matters rather than merely being tidy: the prose was also wrong in each case. The `agent` list claimed `tom_basics`, which no file in the module imports, and omitted `dart:async`, `cancellation.dart` and `placeholders`; the `llm` list omitted `dart:async`, `dart:convert` and `prompt_sha256.dart`. A prose list can be wrong in a way nothing reads; that is the whole argument for one shape. All 59 modules pass. Zero is the expected steady state -- a fault is repaired by writing the row, never by dropping the section.

check_module_readme_shape.note: Zero from the day it landed: the one readme of 53 that was missing three of the four elements gained them in the same pass. Four packages are in scope. Zero is the expected steady state — a fault is repaired by writing the missing element, never by relaxing the shape.

check_open_ends.note: 31 of the 79 module documents carry no `### What is still open` section. It was 43 on the day completion/README.md stopped calling the section optional; eleven modules were assessed in the same campaign and their documents gained one each -- groups, resource_auth, theme, widget_base, widgets, and tom_core_agentic's agent, isolate_streaming, llm, mcp_auth, bearer_auth and placeholders. The number is held rather than driven to zero in one pass, because writing 43 sections at once would assert 43 assessments nobody performed -- which is the artifact the requirement exists to prevent. The section is written when the unit is assessed, so each scan that completes one lowers this by one and the ratchet then requires the drop be recorded. Faults are MISSING (no heading) plus EMPTY (a heading with nothing under it); EMPTY is zero today and is the cheap way to satisfy MISSING without saying anything, so it is counted from the start rather than added after someone does it. The index and the contract are skipped by name -- neither is a document about a module. tom_flutter_ui_test_app_changes.md gained its section on 2026-09-25 (32 -> 31). tom_core_codespecs_package_new.md gained its section on 2026-09-30 (31 -> 30): assessed against the package at HEAD, the ten tcscan73 findings recorded with their outcomes, none open.

check_open_ends_ledger.note: Lands at zero because the five faults it was written for were repaired in the same pass. `check_open_ends.py` asks whether a unit's open-ends section is there; this asks whether it is still true. A section is written once, when the unit is assessed, and every todo filed against that unit afterwards is a fact it does not know -- so the two drift with nothing between them. That is not hypothetical: the mcp_auth section said "Nothing is open" one turn after it was written, with three todos filed and unworked on the same unit. The join is exact rather than heuristic: a document is <project>_<module>_{new,changes}.md and a todo carries scope.project and scope.module, so the two meet on one equality and no prose is read to decide what a document is about. 45 sections against 2182 todos. Two of the three repaired sections said literally "Nothing." while the corpus held four unclosed todos between them -- tcopen432, tcopen433 and tcfinal21 on kernel/security, tcextension24 on kernel/isolate_pooling -- and the fifth, tcextension20, was missing from a configuration section that already listed eight items. A todo whose scope.files names the completion document is out of scope for it: tcopen345 asks for that very section to exist, and a section naming it would report itself as an open end forever. That is a rule about what the todo is about rather than an exemption list, so the next one needs no edit here. What an item says about the todos it names is check_open_lists.py's question, not this gate's. Zero is the expected steady state; a fault is repaired by writing the item, never by deleting the section.

check_overview_inventory.note: Zero from the day it landed. The quest overview's Package Inventory table and its per-package Structure lines had drifted (the kernel's test-file count was off by fifteen); the recount that introduced this gate fixed every row, stated the counting rules beside the table, and this holds them: each count is recomputed from git-tracked files by the same rules, for the table and for the six Structure lines.

check_readme_status.note: Lands at zero because the two version drifts it found were repaired in the same pass (tom_core_kernel claimed 1.1.1 against a pubspec at 1.1.16, tom_flutter_ui 1.0.0 against 1.1.0) and every test count was removed rather than corrected. The asymmetry is the point: a version is held true because a reader acts on it and a file read checks it, while a count is forbidden because nothing connects it to the suite — tom_core_server's had drifted twice, most recently to 95 suites against 103. See _copilot_guidelines/component_module_readme_example.md §2.

check_reflection_artifacts.note: Zero from the day it landed, because the fourteen stale artifacts it was written for were regenerated in the same pass. 35 artifacts across 18 packages are in scope. Zero is the expected steady state: the gate exists for recurrence, and a fault here is always repaired by regenerating, never by editing the file it names.

check_sample_account_rosters.note: Zero is the steady state, reached in the pass that introduced the checker: its first run found advanced_app_server/README.md's account table listing four of the six auth_db accounts (no dave, no erin), repaired then. Nine marked regions across the sample READMEs (5 auth-db, 2 app-offline, 2 admin-offline) against rosters read from the seeds (auth-db 6 accounts, app-offline 5, admin-offline 4). `--self-test` drops a name from, plants a foreign name in, and plants the reserved phrase in every region, so a zero here means the checker is reading.

check_section_refs.note: Zero, and held there across every package rather than the one it started on. 1773 files: the Dart under lib/, test/, example/, bin/ and tool/ and the shipped prose of all nine packages — tom_core_kernel among them, which the checker had never been pointed at when it was written, and which is 286 of that count. Every shipped comment either says what it means in its own words or names the document its section number belongs to. A bare '§7.2' or 'Phase 2a §16' indexes a quest plan that ships with neither the package nor its tests, so a reader of the shipped artefact cannot resolve it; the next one to arrive is a failure. Zero means something only because the gate also refuses the *marked* form — 'bug §77', 'tests §61(e)' — outright, before it asks whether a document is in view, and because --self-test exercises all thirteen rules: five of the six resolve rather than fault, so a regex that stopped matching would read as a repository that got cleaner. The guards that enforce this convention from inside the test run are covered rather than exempted: a reference inside an inline code span is an exhibit and is skipped, which is what let the one by-filename exemption go and closed the last difference between this gate's file population and check_section_numbers.py's.

check_shared_chrome.note: Zero from the day it landed, which took six repairs. Eight groups of file are copied between packages on purpose -- the four showcase samples' chrome, the DTO reflection helpers, the client-local login credentials -- and every copy now names its whole group in its header comment. Two demo_box.dart copies named each other and not the third, so a developer editing either was told about one other copy out of two; two further groups were identical in code and declared nowhere at all. Both halves of the rule earn their place: the declaration carries showcase_cell.dart's fourth copy, which has drifted in code, and content discovery found the two groups no declaration mentioned. The next copy to arrive undeclared, or the next pointer to fall out of step with its siblings, is a failure.

check_source_citations.note: Holds at zero across a scope that widened twice. Markdown was first excluded outright (173 citations in tom_core_samples), then admitted for that subtree once they had been rewritten by hand to name declarations, and now covers every document that navigates -- doc/ pages, package READMEs and the sample guides, 177 files against the previous 39. The widening cost twelve repairs, nine of them in doc/ pages shipped to consumers, and one was the class of failure this gate exists for: form_authorizers.md cited tom_authorization.dart:352 for `class TomAuthorizer`, which is a doc comment belonging to a different class eighty lines above it -- resolving, fluent and wrong. Three sites named their target and cited a line as well, and one cited `(line 151)` into a file that had since been deleted; both are the argument against validating the numbers rather than removing them. CHANGELOGs, _copilot_guidelines/ and the repo's own README stay out, each for a stated reason rather than a suppression entry -- the last so the suite can go on quoting the shapes it forbids.

check_suite_figures.note: Lands at zero: the nine figures and eleven embed sites already followed the convention, which is exactly why it is pinned before a tenth figure arrives. It guards the three silent failures of a figure store - a figure nobody embeds (ORPHAN), an embed naming a file that is gone (DANGLING), and the inventory in tom_core_samples/assets/README.md disagreeing with the tree or with who actually embeds each figure (INVENTORY) - plus the convention itself: every embed site's <!-- Figure --> comment above and Text / mermaid equivalent disclosure below (SITE), alt text that is a sentence (ALT), and every SVG's viewBox and opening description comment (SVG). Its first run reported figure 09 as an orphan: A1's alt text holds projectRoleFieldGrades[role], balanced brackets CommonMark allows, and the embed pattern had not. The pattern allows one level of nesting now. --self-test plants each of the six faults in the real files and restores them.
